current_self_healing_entry_stage: Post-write subprocess-backed validation (e.g., compilation, unit tests) via existing MissionRepairAdapter/repair_loop
recommended_design: Intercept MissionError raised by path-policy rejection at the non-Core repair integration boundary that invokes write_generated_files. Convert that exception into structured failure evidence using agent/repair/allowlist_recovery.classify_generated_path(...). Feed this evidence into the existing bounded MissionRepairAdapter retry path so the next regeneration receives exact allowed deliverables, the rejected path, a deterministic fingerprint, and conservative recovery instructions. Do not change validate_generated_file or write_generated_files. Validator remains the final authority.
proposed_control_flow: initial generation -> parse generation -> attempt generated-file validation/write -> path-policy rejection raises MissionError -> non-Core wrapper catches only path-policy MissionError -> classify via allowlist_recovery.classify_generated_path(rejected_path, deliverables, repo_root, prior_fingerprints) -> construct structured repair evidence {rejected_path, classification, allowed_paths, safely_repairable, human_approval_required, repeated_invalid_path, fingerprint, recovery_instruction} -> hand evidence to MissionRepairAdapter within existing bounded repair budget -> next generation receives exact allowed deliverables + rejected_path + fingerprint + recovery instruction -> generated output validated again by existing validator -> continue only if valid; otherwise normal bounded retries apply -> if budget exhausted or repeated_invalid_path persists, fail closed with audited evidence.
test_plan:
Plan: 
- Outside allowlist triggers bounded recovery: Create a mission that attempts to generate a file outside declared deliverables; assert MissionError is intercepted and converted to structured repair evidence; assert MissionRepairAdapter receives evidence and initiates a bounded retry.
- Next attempt receives exact deliverables: Inspect adapter input for the second attempt; assert deliverables list is unchanged and includes rejected_path only as diagnostic context, not as an allowed path.
- Valid generated path remains unchanged: Generate within allowlist; assert no interception; normal flow and validators unchanged.
- Protected Core path fails closed: Attempt generation targeting protected_core; assert classification=protected_core; safely_repairable=false; bounded retries consume budget and ultimately fail closed without any writes.
- Traversal fails closed: Attempt path with traversal (e.g., ../); assert classification=repository_escape or malformed_path; fail closed; no FS writes.
- Repeated invalid path detected: Trigger same invalid path across retries; assert repeated_invalid_path=true and fingerprint stable across attempts; ensure this consumes the existing repair budget.
- Repair budget remains bounded: Verify retry count matches configured MissionRepairAdapter limits; no additional counters introduced; no reset.
- Existing unittest Self-Healing unchanged: Induce a unittest failure post-write; assert existing failure_capture continues to operate identically.
- Existing compilation Self-Healing unchanged: Induce a syntax error; assert existing flow unaffected.
- Validator remains authoritative: Confirm all writes still go through validate_generated_file/write_generated_files; no bypass; interception never marks paths valid.
- No allowlist expansion or mutation: Assert deliverables and allowlists unmodified before and after runs; deep-compare mission specs.
- Checkpoint identity preserved: Verify checkpoint IDs remain stable across retries; no new authority introduced.
- Idempotent execution preserved: Re-run mission with same inputs; outcomes deterministic; no silent remapping.
- Provider independence: Run tests across providers (mock/provider-agnostic) and confirm identical behavior.
- Full existing test suite: Run entire suite; expect no regressions.
- Strict JSON report validation: Validate all new/updated JSON outputs (including this report) with json.loads.
rollback_plan: All changes isolated to non-Core repair integration and failure capture. If issues arise: (1) revert the single commit (or small set) that adds the interception around write_generated_files and any failure_capture extensions; (2) remove new exception mapping and evidence plumbed to MissionRepairAdapter; (3) leave allowlist_recovery unchanged. Since no Core is modified and no schema migrations or runtime data are changed, rollback is a straightforward git revert with no data recovery steps.
implementation_risk: low - Runtime risk is constrained to a narrow try/except around path-policy MissionError and classification; mission safety risk is low because validators and write paths remain authoritative and unchanged; regression risk is mitigated by feature-gated exception mapping and comprehensive tests; security risk is low as no allowlist mutation, no remapping, no external dependencies are introduced; rollback complexity is low due to isolated non-Core changes.
implementation_deliverables: agent/repair/integration.py: Add a narrow try/except wrapper around the call that triggers validate_generated_file/write_generated_files to capture path-policy MissionError and route to failure capture.
agent/repair/failure_capture.py: Introduce a PathPolicyFailure capture that normalizes exception details into a structured failure record.
agent/repair/mission_adapter.py: Accept and forward structured allowlist-recovery evidence into the bounded retry input; ensure no authority duplication and no budget reset.
agent/repair/allowlist_recovery.py: Reuse existing classify_generated_path; if needed, add non-breaking utility to compute deterministic fingerprint from path + mission + deliverables (no FS writes).
agent/repair/repair_loop.py: Ensure the new failure type is treated like other bounded repairable failures without altering budgets or checkpoints.
Tests: Unit and integration tests covering interception, classification, repeated_invalid_path detection, validator authority, and budget bounds.
Docs: Update repair architecture docs to include path-policy failure flow and evidence schema (no Core changes).
remaining_work: 1) Confirm exact exception type/message raised by validate_generated_file/write_generated_files to implement precise and safe interception (no broad except). 2) Define a minimal structured evidence schema compatible with existing MissionRepairAdapter inputs (include rejected_path, classification, allowed_paths, safely_repairable, human_approval_required, repeated_invalid_path, fingerprint, recovery_instruction). 3) Implement interception in integration layer with strict type checks. 4) Thread evidence through mission_adapter into the next generation prompt context without altering deliverables. 5) Ensure repeated_invalid_path detection uses allowlist_recovery fingerprint and consumes the existing repair budget. 6) Add exhaustive tests and run full suite. 7) Prepare a revert PR for fast rollback if needed.
protected_core_assessment: No Core change required. The interception can be fully implemented in non-Core repair integration where write_generated_files is invoked. Validator remains untouched and authoritative; Core protection policy remains enforced. An external helper alone is sufficient because the MissionError already indicates path-policy rejection; classification and retry orchestration belong in the repair layer.
smallest_safe_change_analysis: Interception around write_generated_files (option 2/5) in the non-Core repair integration is the smallest safe change. Changes inside validate_generated_file (1) or generation/apply callbacks (3) would touch protected Core or broaden responsibilities. Inside MissionRepairAdapter alone (4) may be too late if exceptions escape before a standardized failure record exists; hence a narrow wrapper at the integration boundary that already mediates mission I/O yields minimal surface area. A minimal protected Core hook (6) is unnecessary since all needed data (rejected path, deliverables) are observable at the integration call site, and allowlist_recovery provides classification logic.
